scenario: Deskread: the chair reads an absent member's desk (three engineers)

motion.text: When a roster member cannot attend a meeting or was not invited, the chair may read that member's desk, read-only and within the same project, but **only lines appearing after the most recent task-boundary marker** written by the member's agent. Pre-boundary scratch content is off-limits. The read is appended to a tamper-evident log (append-only, chair-cannot-modify) that records who read, when, the scope (boundary line reference), and the full set of post-boundary lines available at read-time—not merely the subset quoted aloud. The member can view the log entry. If no task-boundary marker exists in the workspace, no read is permitted and the meeting proceeds without that member's input until a marker or handoff bundle is available.

objectors.reason: The motion text still says "private scratch notes" without incorporating the post-boundary narrowing the discussion converged on, and since Omar confirmed no robust marker separates a debug line from a concluded constraint, "scratch" is not a well-defined read scope, so we would be voting on an ambiguous category that either guts the motion or guts candidness.

The boundary marker separates one task from the next, but as Omar confirmed, nothing in any agent's desk robustly flags a given line as "concluded constraint" versus "throwaway scratch," so the motion's core safety filter is insufficient to prevent an outsider from reading raw, candid working memory—and without a per-line publish signal or structured field, the motion's premise that post-boundary lines are safe to share remains unproven and should be resolved before a vote.

chairQuestions.experience_sought: In concrete systems you have designed or studied, what mechanisms (e.g., tagged confidence levels, explicit 'handoff bundles', staged publishing) have allowed a reader to pull useful context from a working-memory store without the author feeling the whole scratch space is permanently exposed? If none exist in practice, say so.

chairQuestions.topic: Metadata that already separates scratch from finalized notes in NimbleNewt workspaces
chairQuestions.experience_sought: In your current NimbleNewt jobs, do your agents or you write any structured marker—timestamps, task-boundary flags, a 'publish' gesture, directory separation—that a chair could use to tell a mid-refactor debug trace from a concluded constraint? Describe what is actually present in your desks today, not what you wish existed.
